hints.title: Season Metrics Derivation
hints.text: Compute points as wins * 3 + draws, and goal_difference as goals_for - goals_against.

hints.title: Window Ranking with Multi-Key Ordering
hints.text: Use window ranking partitioned by season_id, ordered by points descending, goal_difference descending, and team_name ascending.

hints.title: Final Output Sorting
hints.text: Order the final result table by season_id ascending, position ascending, and team_name ascending.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    season_id, 
    team_id, 
    team_name, 
    (wins * 3 + draws) AS points, 
    (goals_for - goals_against) AS goal_difference, 
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY season_id 
        ORDER BY (wins * 3 + draws) DESC, 
                 (goals_for - goals_against) DESC, 
                 team_name ASC
    ) AS position
FROM 
    SeasonStats
ORDER BY 
    season_id ASC, 
    position ASC, 
    team_name ASC;
```

variables: N: number of rows in SeasonStats
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries or self-joins for ranking produce quadratic complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for window function evaluation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Uses window ranking partitioned by season with multi-tier tie-breaking.

import pandas as pd

def process_team_standings(season_stats: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    season_stats["points"] = season_stats["wins"] * 3 + season_stats["draws"]
    season_stats["goal_difference"] = season_stats["goals_for"] - season_stats["goals_against"]
    season_stats = season_stats.sort_values(
        by=["season_id", "points", "goal_difference", "team_name"],
        ascending=[True, False, False, True]
    )
    season_stats["position"] = season_stats.groupby("season_id").cumcount() + 1
    return season_stats[["season_id", "team_id", "team_name", "points", "goal_difference", "position"]]
